# Run the pipeline

To start the pipeline, press **Update**. The run window says how many samples will run and shows the
Nextflow command:

![The run window, with the number of samples to run and the Nextflow command](figures/get-started/update-window.png)

**Resume previous run?** reuses work so that a
stopped or failed run picks up where it left off. Leave it ticked.

Press **Run from App**. Progress shows in the window, one line per step:

::: {.alert .alert-hydra}
[HYDRA]{.hydra-tag} **Submit as job.** Press **Submit as job** in place of
**Run from App**; see [Submit a run as a job](Clusters.html#submit-a-run-as-a-job).
:::

![Progress of a running pipeline](figures/get-started/run-progress.png)

::: {.alert .alert-warning}
**Keep this browser tab open and the computer awake while running the pipeline.**
Closing the tab or pressing **Stop** stops the run; see
[Stopping and resuming a run](Troubleshooting.html#stopping-and-resuming-a-run).
:::

One pipeline run does everything for each sample: it cleans the reads, assembles the
rDNA, picks and scores the contigs, compares them with GenBank, maps the reads
back to compute depth statistics, annotates the five features, runs the quality checks, and proposes
which contigs to keep. The test run takes about 20 minutes.

When the run ends, the app reports how it went. A clean run says "Run finished
with no failures." Otherwise it shows a report that names every sample that
failed. In the test project one sample fails on purpose:

![End-of-run summary naming the sample that failed](figures/get-started/run-finished.png)

If a step of the pipeline stops with an error, the report also names the
sample, the step, the error code, and the likely cause. The [Troubleshooting](Troubleshooting.html) page
explains how to interpret the report in more detail.

You can examine these reports later by clicking the **Run Reports** button in the top right
corner of the app.

# Examine the results

The Assemble table has one row per sample:

![The Assemble table after the first run](figures/get-started/assemble-table.png)

The columns to look at first:

- **State**: a green check means the sample finished; a red triangle means it
  failed. Hover over the icon to see what it means.
- **Lock**: shows an open lock icon until you lock the sample.
- **Checks**: summary of all quality checks for the sample.
  Red means a potentially serious issue, amber is worth a look but possibly benign,
  green is ok, and gray means there was nothing to compare with. See
  [The Checks column](Curation-Flags.html#the-checks-column).
- **# Paths**, **# Contigs**, and **# Kept**: how many assembly paths and
  contigs the assembly produced, and how many contigs are kept. 0 kept contigs means
  there is nothing to export.
- **ITSx Warnings**: shows any issues reported by the ITSx check; see
  [the ITSx check](GenBank-Submission.html#check-before-you-submit).
- **Notes**: what the pipeline noted about the sample, for example why it
  failed.
- **User Notes**: your own notes on the sample, typed in the **Notes** box at
  the bottom of its details window.

In the Assemble step, you mostly choose which contigs to keep or drop.
Trimming contigs and adjusting gene boundaries happens in the Annotation Review step.

RiboPilot runs a triage process during the pipeline
that automatically keeps or drops contigs. Use the **Triage** button at the top of the app
to modify how the triage rules work and run the process again for selected samples.
[Quality checks and flags](Curation-Flags.html) explains the triage rules.

# View sample assembly details

Click a sample's ID to open its details. This window lists the sample's
contigs, each with **K** (keep) and **D** (drop) buttons, as well as other 
information like coverage, features annotated, and the verdict
from the BLAST screen. 

Clicking a contig row in the table highlights that row in blue. The
**BLAST evidence**, **Coverage and windowed BLAST**, and **Windowed BLAST details** 
panels all show information for the highlighted contig.

CHIM01 is an artificial chimeric contig, crated by joining sequence data from
*Penicillium* mold and the fish species *Upeneus parvus*.
The BLAST evidence shows that the best overall match is a *Penicillium* mold:

![CHIM01's BLAST evidence, with its best match a Penicillium mold](figures/get-started/assemble-details-chim01.png)

The **Coverage and windowed BLAST** viewer shows more detail about the chimeric sequence.
In the **BLAST origin** track, segments are colored by BLAST taxonomic match (gray is
the sample's own lineage, yellow in this case represents the mold sequence).
A dashed red line marks approximate position of the join between the fish
and the mold sequences, near 2,625 bp. You can hover over the track to see more details. 

The **Windowed BLAST details** panel provides more detail about the BLAST results for each
section of the chimeric contig.

![CHIM01 in the sequence viewer, with the join between the fish and the mold marked](figures/get-started/assemble-chimera-chim01.png)

# Rescue a sample that failed

One sample in the test project is expected to fail: every contig assembled for SRR22396893
is shorter than the default 500 bp minimum. Its State shows a red
triangle. The sample's details window shows additional information:

![Details of a failed sample, with the reason and the next step](figures/get-started/failed-sample.png)

To try fixing the failed sample:

1. Click that sample's **Assembly Options** cell.
2. Type a new name in **Parameter set name**, for example `baited`, and tick
   **Edit**.
3. Under **Assembler**, choose **SPAdes, baited to the seed DB**.
4. Press **Save**. The sample is set to Ready to run.
5. Press **Update**, then **Run from App**.

![Assembly options set to the baited SPAdes assembler](figures/get-started/rescue-baited.png)

::: {.alert .alert-hydra}
[HYDRA]{.hydra-tag} **CPUs and memory are per-job requests.** On Hydra the
**CPUs** and **Memory (GB)** in an options window become each job's request to
the scheduler. A request of more than 8 GB per CPU is flagged as a high-memory
job automatically. See the
[Hydra wiki](https://confluence.si.edu/spaces/HPC/pages/163152285/Compute+Nodes)
for the compute nodes on offer.
:::

When the run finishes, open SRR22396893's details again. Baited SPAdes recovers
four contigs over 500 bp, but none spans the whole 18S-to-28S region.
Read depth for all of the contigs is low, which is likely why the we cannot assemble a larger contig.

![Baited SPAdes contigs for SRR22396893: four partial pieces of 18S, ITS1, and 28S](figures/get-started/assemble-details-baited.png)

For more information about assemblers in RiboPilot, see [Choosing an assembly method](Assembly-Methods.html)

# Lock samples when done

Select one or more samples and press **Lock**. Locked samples now appear in the Annotation Review
step. For this test run, lock all 12 passing samples. When Lock asks about
CHIM01, press **Lock anyway**, so you can see how the Export step will warn you about problematic contigs.
